is-ui-holding-us-back.title: Who does the work?
is-ui-holding-us-back.description: Conceptual routes to the same outcome. Direct controls leave navigation with the person; API/CLI calls specify operations; WebMCP exposes page actions; voice supplies an instruction. Voice through MCP is our proposed next experiment. The routes coexist and are not a ranking of speed or accessibility.

web-accessibility-can-people-finish.title: The scan is only the beginning
web-accessibility-can-people-finish.description: WebAIM found detected WCAG failures on 95.9% of the one million home pages evaluated in February 2026. Each cell represents one percentage point; one is 90% filled. The remaining 4.1% had no detected failures, which does not establish accessibility. The scan does not measure independent task completion.

webmcp-actions-on-the-page.title: Choose where the work belongs
webmcp-actions-on-the-page.description: The page boundary contains the person, the controls, browser-agent tool calls and shared app actions. A separate service path connects an assistant through an MCP server to an API. These are different scopes; neither guarantees accessibility or replaces authorisation.

hands-free-app-control.title: A result earns its reply
hands-free-app-control.description: In the documented Cargo workflow, a spoken request initiates recovery. The officer checks the sandbox service until it answers twice before reporting recovery. This depicts the recorded implementation, not a new run, participant study or general performance result.

voice-through-mcp.title: One request, separate permissions
voice-through-mcp.description: An illustrative request to prepare a release note reaches an assistant. It could read blockers through one MCP server and create a draft through another. Each service checks its own scope. Sending is a separate decision. This cross-app path has not been executed for the series.

future-ui-keep-your-place.title: Change the input, keep the work
future-ui-keep-your-place.description: The shortlist, its evidence and the person’s decisions remain at the centre. Speech, keyboard, screen-reader output and direct controls can provide routes into the same task. This is a design goal that requires implementation and evaluation, not an observed cross-modal result.
